Quiet.md 

 
 A fast, quiet, local notes app. 
 Drawn natively with Rust + GPUI. Your notes stay on your computer, stored in the Feishu (Lark) DocxXML format.
 

 
 English · 简体中文 · 日本語 · 한국어 · Español · Français 
 

 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 
 
  
 
  
 
 

 
 Website ·
 Download ·
 Performance ·
 Features ·
 Contributing 
 

 
 
 

 [!NOTE]
 Quiet.md is in beta and changing quickly. If you hit a bug or have an idea, please open an issue — or better, send a pull request.

 Why Quiet.md

 ⚡ Fast, the native kind of fast. The whole interface is drawn on the GPU by Rust and GPUI. No WebView, no Electron. In a one-million-character document, typing, deleting and scrolling all stay under 6 ms per frame at P95.

 🔒 Local-first. Your files are yours. No account, no cloud, and nothing goes over the network by default (the optional update check aside). Your library is an ordinary folder on your computer: the sidebar's folders are real folders, and each note is a file named by its title ( .xml , or .md for Markdown). Manage it with Git, iCloud or any sync tool you like; if you ever stop using Quiet.md, your files are still there.

 📝 A full rich-text editor that speaks Feishu (Lark) DocxXML. Notes are saved in the DocxXML format used by Feishu (Lark) Docs, so copy-paste, import and export keep their structure. Headings, to-dos, tables, columns, callouts, code, math, images and attachments — the blocks you reach for when writing documents are all there.

 Download

 
 
  
 
  
 
 

 Platform Package Requirements 
 --- --- --- 
 macOS (Apple Silicon) quiet-md-macos-arm64.zip macOS 13 or later 
 Windows (x64) quiet-md-windows-x64-setup.exe Windows 10 version 1809 or later 
 Linux (x86 64, experimental) quiet-md-x86 64.AppImage glibc 2.35 or later (Ubuntu 22.04 and newer) 
 macOS (Intel) quiet-md-macos-x86 64.zip macOS 13 or later 

- macOS : unzip and drag quiet.md.app into Applications. The app is signed and notarized by Apple.
- Windows : run the installer. By default it installs for the current user only, and uninstalling never deletes your notes. If SmartScreen appears on first launch, click More info → Run anyway .
- Linux (experimental): chmod +x quiet-md- .AppImage and run it; without FUSE, add --appimage-extract-and-run . AppImage 0.1.10 and later support in-app updates; older Linux versions need a one-time manual install. Interactive testing so far covers Omarchy on Wayland; see the Linux notes.

You can also download from Quiet.md. Every release and its SHA-256 checksums are on GitHub Releases.

On first launch, Quiet.md asks for the interface language, where to keep your library and the quick-note shortcut, and offers to copy in notes from Obsidian, Logseq, iA Writer or Typora. An empty library gets a Getting started guide — a ten-minute tour of the main features. Existing notes are never overwritten.

The interface is available in English, Simplified Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Spanish, French and Arabic.

 Performance

Frame processing time over 100 consecutive operations in a mixed document of 1 million characters and 549 chapters:

 Operation P50 P95 
 --- ---: ---: 
 ⌨️ Typing 5.06 ms 5.78 ms 
 ⌫ Backspace 4.99 ms 5.55 ms 
 🖱️ Scrolling 2.08 ms 4.14 ms 

A 120 Hz display gives each frame 8.3 ms. Even at P95 on a million-character document, there is headroom left.

 
 --- --- 
 macOS download 18 MB 
 Windows installer 14 MB 
 Runtime No WebView, no Electron, no background services 

 Apple M5 Pro / 48 GiB, macOS 26.5, release build. Methodology and scripts to reproduce: docs/PERFORMANCE.md. 

 Features

- Editing : headings, ordered and bulleted lists, to-dos, quotes, code blocks with syntax highlighting, LaTeX math, tables (with merged cells), callouts, columns, images, attachments and covers. Markdown shortcuts such as , - , [] and , plus a / slash menu.
- Boards : a whiteboard ported from Excalidraw — shapes, arrows that stay bound, freehand, text, sticky notes, frames and images — as a block in a note or a standalone .excalidraw file that excalidraw.com opens.
- Version history : each note keeps snapshots of its previous contents as it saves (20 by default, 1–30 under Settings › Documents). A drawer lists them by day; clicking one shows that version in place, read-only, with the blocks it added or rewrote tinted and a one-click restore. Important versions can be named.
- Organizing : a document tree, pinning, favorites, full-text search and a trash.
- Import and export : import Markdown folders (Obsidian picture embeds and callouts included) and Feishu (Lark) DocxXML; export Markdown and PDF, or print directly. Drag files from Finder onto Home or straight into a sidebar folder. Pasting from Feishu or a web page keeps the structure.
- Shortcuts : press ⌘ / ( Ctrl+/ on Windows) to see them all. Every one can be rebound. On Windows, Ctrl stands in for ⌘ and Alt for ⌥; the app and the Getting started guides show the keys for your system.
- Themes : four built-in styles — Craft, Feishu, Notion and Obsidian — each with a dark variant, or write your own in CSS; see docs/THEMES.md.

 Contributors

Thanks to everyone who has helped build Quiet.md. Issues and pull requests are welcome: building, testing and code conventions are in CONTRIBUTING.md.

 

 Recent updates

- 0.1.13 (Nov 17): boards — a whiteboard ported from Excalidraw, as a block in a note or a standalone .excalidraw file, fast with 10,000 shapes. Version history for every note (… › Version history). French and Arabic interfaces. Copy as Markdown, copy a file's path, and switch the library folder in Settings. Pasted web images are saved into the library. Less memory on picture-heavy pages and smoother sidebar scrolling.
- 0.1.12 (Nov 14): drag files from Finder, or a file from Files on this computer, straight into a sidebar folder or between rows; the whole page lights up as a drop target. Redesigned Home cards with squircle corners, an Open in Finder menu, breadcrumbs that start at My documents, a minimum window
